chunks: And Hammad narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:

Regarding a mukātab who enters into a contract of emancipation, and whose masters stipulate against him that if he becomes unable, then he is owned, and whatever they have taken from him belongs to them, he said: "His masters take him according to their condition."

key_terms.الْمُكَاتَبِ: a slave under a contractual agreement of emancipation
key_terms.عَجَزَ: he became unable to fulfill the required payment or obligation
key_terms.مَمْلُوكٌ: owned; returned to the status of property/slavery
key_terms.مَوَالِيهِ: his masters or patrons who hold authority over him
key_terms.يَشْتَرِطُ: he stipulates a condition in the contract

ai.seo_question: If a mukātab fails to fulfill his manumission contract, do his masters take him back according to the stipulated condition?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a mukātab, a slave under a manumission contract, when the masters stipulate that failure to complete payment returns him to bondage. Imam Abu Abdullah عليه السلام states that the condition is enforced, and the masters reclaim him according to what they stipulated.
